column2: RESOLVED. An earlier pass left these split on the grounds that "the only consequence is
whether the click sound plays". That was wrong, and the game proved it: TScreen.
CheckInput's Case 5 runs `PlaySound(g_sndclick, ...)` BEFORE `g_activegadget.fHit()`,
and g_sndclick is read there and written NOWHERE in the corpus. So it was Null, and
PlaySound(Null, chan) faulted -- an access violation on EVERY click, the moment mouse
input started working. A split is not automatically cosmetic just because the value it
loses is; what matters is what dereferences it.
Resolution, by elimination rather than by guessing which sound is nicer:
* g_snd_select appears under THAT SAME NAME in both TScreen.SetUp (which loads
Sounds/Select.ogg into it) and TTable.UpdateActivated. So that name is already
unified across the corpus and needs no merge.
* TTable.UpdateActivated.bmx:25-27 pins the two TSound slots in order --
"0x00C61720 and 0x00C6171C -> TSound ... Named g_chan_ui / g_snd_move /
g_snd_select here" -- giving 0x00C61720 = g_snd_move, 0x00C6171C = g_snd_select.
* TScreen.CheckInput.bmx:5 pins its own g_sndclick pragma to 0x00C6171C.
0x00C6171C is g_snd_select, therefore g_sndclick IS g_snd_select.
* TScreen.SetUp writes exactly two TSounds (g_snd_click = Click.ogg,
g_snd_select = Select.ogg) and there are exactly two UI TSound slots. With
g_snd_select taken by 0x00C6171C, g_snd_click can only be 0x00C61720 -- which
TTable calls g_snd_move.
The result is also behaviourally sensible, which is a check on the reasoning rather
than the reason for it: moving between items plays Click.ogg (g_snd_move, 4 call sites
in TTable, all movement), and activating something plays Select.ogg (g_snd_select, in
TTable's activation branch and in CheckInput's gadget-hit branch).

column2: Reported symptoms, all one defect: "difficulty buttons do nothing", "sound FX buttons
don't work", "currency doesn't work", "when I turned music off it didn't preserve my
choice", "match time buttons crash", "distance yards/metres instantly crashes".
Three layers touch each option and each was recovered with its OWN name for the slot:
TOptions.LoadOptions / SaveOptions   the persistence layer   -> g_opt_<thing>
TScreen_Options.Button<Thing>        the click handler       -> some other name
TScreen_Options.RefreshButtons       the redraw              -> a third name
So a click stored the value where nothing read it, the redraw kept showing the old
state, and Save wrote the untouched persisted copy back to Options.ini. Measured: of 20
Options handlers, only 4 (BossFx, MatchFx, ShowEnergy, ToolTips) happened to agree with
RefreshButtons on the name -- which matches the reported "some work, most don't" exactly.
CANONICAL = the name TOptions.LoadOptions/SaveOptions uses. That layer decides whether a
setting survives a restart, so unifying onto anything else would fix the UI and leave
persistence broken.

column2: ---- 0x00C67B90 : the contract-offer accept callback ----------------------------------
TScreen_ContractOffer.ButtonAccept.bmx (byte-identical 34/34) calls it unconditionally
as g_fnAccept:Int(), an Int() Global with no initializer anywhere in the corpus --
BlitzMax stamps an unassigned Int() Global with the runtime's NullFunctionError
thrower, so this call always throws. That same body reads the dword at 0x00c67b88
into eax (the g_contractoffer slot), then calls through the dword at 0x00c67b90 --
a bare indirect call through a Global, not a class-table dispatch.
TScreen_ContractOffer.SetUpScreen.bmx (byte-identical 418/418) writes that
same slot with a bare mov and no refcount traffic at line 66, `g_co_fn2 = a2`, fed from
its SIG=(:TContractOffer,()i,()i)i third parameter; its own header independently
derives "0x00C67B90 Int() g_co_fn2". TScreen_NewPlayer.DoClubTrial.bmx:111 is the
new-career call site and passes TProfile.StartNewGame as that same a2 argument, so the
value g_fnAccept needed was already being written one call earlier under a different
name. No co-occurrence conflict (the two names never appear in the same body); both
declared Int(). scripts/unify_names.py's slot_kinds() drops any address seen only as
PTR_FUN_ (built to exclude class-table call targets), so validate_verdicts.py's
automated ADDRESS check cannot see either side of this call and rejects the pin on a
function-pointer Global structurally, not on the evidence; four independent verdict
rounds (extracted/unify_work/verdicts.json, verdicts_all.json, verdicts_round3.json,
verdicts_dead93.json) reached this same RESOLVED merge_into=g_co_fn2 conclusion, and
verdicts_dead93.json's evidence already names the PTR_FUN filtering as the cause.

column2: ---- 0x00C6F08C : the music channel, and why music=0 crashed the trial ---------------
The reported crash after the Pace training set up: a `-d` build reported
Attempt to access field or method of Null object immediately after
LogLine("ResumeSounds"), which is the FIRST statement of TEngine.ResumeSounds, so the
fault is inside it. For a training (g_training_int03 <> 0) that body runs only its last
three statements: ResumeChannel on channels 4, 5 and 6.
TEngine.ResumeSounds is byte-identical and its header lists the six channel slots it
touches, in touch order: 0x00C5B340, 0x00C5B344, 0x00C5B348, 0x00C5B33C, 0x00C600D4,
0x00C6F08C. TEngine.SetUpChannels is also byte-identical and allocates exactly the
FIRST FIVE of those. The sixth, 0x00C6F08C, it does not -- that one is the music
channel, and the module body allocates it unconditionally at start-up
(`g_Object858 = AllocChannel()`, address recorded inline at
src/recovered_unverified/ModuleBody_RealProgram.bmx:162).
In our build that one slot survived as TWO Globals:
g_musicchannel  -- what PlayTrack.bmx:17 and UpdateAudio.bmx:19 (both byte-identical)
bind 0x00C6F08C to, and what ResumeSounds reads through g_eng_ch6.
Its ONLY writer is PlayTrack:36.
g_object858     -- what the module body assigns at boot. Also g_snd_chan6 in
TEngine.PauseSounds.
So the boot allocation landed on one variable and every reader looked at the other.
Why it only bites some installs: PlayTrack's first branch is
`If a0 = 0 Or g_musicvol = 0`, which merely Stops the channel -- it never allocates.
The allocation at PlayTrack:36 sits in the ElseIf. With music volume 0 in Options.ini
(the reporting install logs `Load variable: music = 0.000000000`) StartMusic -> PlayTrack(1)
takes the first branch, g_musicchannel is never assigned, and ResumeChannel(Null) throws
-- BRL's ResumeChannel is a bare `channel.SetPaused False`, with no Null guard
(tools/blitzmax-legacy-src/mod/brl.mod/audio.mod/audio.bmx:327).
The ORIGINAL cannot hit this: one slot, allocated at boot, so it is non-Null whatever
the music volume. Turning music up would have masked it, which is exactly the kind of
machine-specific split this table exists to close.
Merged onto g_musicchannel rather than g_object858 because the two byte-identical
bodies that bind the address by name (PlayTrack, UpdateAudio) both spell it that way,
and it carries the meaning. Both names are TChannel, so no type conflict.
NOTE FOR WHOEVER PICKS THIS UP: a sweep for "one address, 2+ surviving Globals" -- NOT
the narrower "one is written and the other never is", which is what missed this one,
since BOTH halves here have a writer -- reports 62 addresses still in this state. Most
need individual adjudication and some are solver noise rather than real splits (0x00000000
carries seven names; g_camerax1/g_cameray1 appear at BOTH 0x00C5DCB0 and 0x00C5DCB4,
which is an unresolved pairing, not an identity). The engine's own audio channels are in
that list and look real -- 0x00C5B340 g_chan_a/g_chn2, 0x00C5B344 g_chan_b/g_channel_sfx,
0x00C5B348 g_chan_c/g_chan_e/g_chn4, 0x00C5B33C g_chan_d/g_chn1 -- and would bite a real
match (TEngine.UpdateSounds' g_training_int03 = 0 branch) the way this one bit training.

column2: ---- 0x00C6CF90 vs 0x00C6CF98 : why KICK never started a training challenge ----------
Symptom: the Pace trial drew, controls bound correctly, but pressing KICK did nothing --
the player could not move and the countdown never ran. TTraining.StartChallenge has
exactly one caller, TEngine.SkipTime:55, and it was unreachable.
TEngine.SkipTime is byte-identical, but a byte match MASKS Global addresses, so it
cannot tell these two apart. The original says plainly:
0x004D75AF  cmp dword ptr [0xc6cf90], 0     <- If g_trainingon <> 0
0x004D75B8  mov eax, dword ptr [0xc6cf98]   <- Select g_trainingmode
0x004D75BD  cmp eax,0 / cmp eax,1 / cmp eax,2
Two DIFFERENT slots: 0x00C6CF90 is "a training is running" (also called g_training,
g_train_mode, g_training_int03 -- it holds the training TYPE, 1 for Pace), and
0x00C6CF98 is the challenge STATE (0 intro, 1 running, 2 done; also g_train_state,
g_training_int05, and what TTraining.StartChallenge writes as g_tr_challenge).
SkipTime.bmx's own header line 9 records this correctly -- "0x00C6CF90 -> g_trainingon
0x00C6CF98 -> g_trainingmode" -- but the alias tables overrode it, because the NAME
g_trainingmode is used for 0x00C6CF90 in other bodies (TBall.HitPost.bmx:17,
TEngine.StartReplay.bmx:4). One name, two addresses, resolved on the name.
Consequences, both fatal to the trial:
* g_trainingon was left as a Global of its own that nothing writes, so it read 0 and
the whole `If g_trainingon <> 0` training branch was skipped -- KICK fell through to
the ordinary match handling, which is why pressing it eventually opened the pause
screen instead.
* g_trainingmode resolved to 0x00C6CF90, whose value during a Pace trial is 1, so the
Select hit the EMPTY Case 1 rather than Case 0's StartChallenge().
Fixed per file rather than by a global merge, since neither name can be bound to one
address corpus-wide.
GDB caught this one directly. Breakpoint on brl_blitz_NullObjectError in a

brl_blitz_NullObjectError <- brl_max2d_DrawImageRect <- TTraining.RenderScoreboard
<- TEngine.Render <- TEngine.RenderGameEngine <- TEngine.MatchLoop <- SetUpMatch
<- TTraining.SetUpTraining <- TScreen_NewPlayer.DoClubTrial

column1: # ---- 2026-08-22: TEngine's five match channels -- REPAIRING THE QUIT CRASH -------------
# Symptom: quitting a training faults with "Attempt to access field or method of Null
# object" inside TEngine.EndMatch -> StopChannels. BRL StopChannel
# (mod/brl.mod/audio.mod/audio.bmx:259) is an unguarded `channel.Stop`, so the very first
# call faults on a Null slot.
# THIS IS A DIRECTION CONFLICT BETWEEN TWO OF THE TABLES ABOVE, not a missing merge.
# The five slots are allocated in TEngine.SetUpChannels (original 0x004CE59B) and released
# in TEngine.StopChannels (original 0x004CE6C3, byte-identical 251/251). Disassembled, the
# allocator is five copies of `If Not <slot> Then <slot> = AllocChannel()` -- cmp against
# 0x005C9C80 (bbNullObject), jne past, call 0x0059B290 = _brl_audio_AllocChannel, then
# `mov [<slot>], ebx` -- over the addresses, in this order:
# which is exactly SetUpChannels.bmx's declaration order g_chan_a, g_chan_b, g_chan_c,
# g_chan_d, g_chan_e. StopChannels touches the SAME five addresses in the SAME order and
# spells them g_chn2, g_chn3, g_chn4, g_chn1, g_chn5.
# global_alias_unified.tsv (prec 1) resolved four of the five toward the StopChannels
# spelling (g_chan_d->g_chn1, g_chan_a->g_chn2, g_chan_b->g_channel_sfx, g_chan_c->g_chn4).
# global_alias_writers.tsv (prec 2) and global_alias_adjudicated.tsv (prec 3) later named
# g_chan_a/b/c/d canonical instead -- ten rows between them. assemble.py's global_alias_map()
# then does the right thing per its own contract: "a name that a HIGHER-precedence table
# calls canonical must not stay an alias in a lower-precedence one", so it DELETES the
# unified edges g_chan_a/b/c/d -> g_chn*. That leaves the g_chn* names as canonicals of
# their own, and each address emits TWO independent Globals: the allocator writes one, the
# teardown reads the other, and the teardown's is Null forever.
# The control is decisive: 0x00C600D4 is the ONE address where unified already chose the
# allocator spelling (g_chn5 -> g_chan_e), so no adjudicated row ever had to override it,
# no edge was deleted, and it never split. In the crash dump
# (status/debugruns/20260822-204758/globals.tsv, captured at fault time) that is exactly
# the one that survives:
#     g_chan_a $33630ea0  g_chan_b $336315c0  g_chan_c $3131f8e0
#     g_chan_d $336332c0  g_chan_e $31d44770        <- all five ALLOCATED
#     g_chn1 Null  g_chn2 Null  g_chn4 Null  g_channel_sfx Null   <- the split halves
# So the channels were never missing; the teardown was reading the wrong four variables.
# DIRECTION. The allocator's spelling is canonical, on four independent grounds: (1)
# SetUpChannels is the ONLY body that stores a channel object into these slots -- every
# other write in the corpus is the `= Null` in StopChannels; (2) link_dead_to_writers.py,
# which aligns assignment targets against the original's store targets, independently
# emitted g_snd_chan2->g_chan_a and g_object46/g_snd_chan4/g_trainingline_chan/g_eng_ch3->
# g_chan_c; (3) all ten adjudicated rows for this family point at g_chan_*; (4) 0x00C600D4,
# the address that works, is already g_chan_e. Pinning here at prec 4 makes the four
# remaining addresses agree with it, and cannot cycle: the override raises
# rank["=g_chan_*"] to 4, so the stale unified edge g_chan_* -> g_chn* is dropped by the
# same de-alias pass that is causing the split today, and the chain collapse then lands
# every name in the group on the allocator's.
# NO GUARD IS MISSING. StopChannels' original is `push [slot]; call 0x0059B2A7` five times
# with NO null test -- and the contrast is visible in the same disassembly, because
# SetUpChannels 40 bytes earlier DOES emit the `cmp eax,0x5C9C80 / setne / movzx / cmp /
# jne` sequence for its `If Not`. The recovered body is faithful and must not be edited.
# The original relies on the same invariant we do: StopChannels is reachable only from
# TEngine.EndMatch, and SetUpChannels is called unconditionally from TEngine.SetUpMatch:126
# and TEngine.SetUpReplay:60, so all five slots are allocated by AllocChannel() whether or
# not any sound ever played. The dump confirms it empirically -- g_chan_a..e are all
# allocated at fault time. Full wiring is the whole fix.
0x00C5B33C

column1: # ---- 2026-08-22: the END-OF-MATCH CALLBACK -- THE NEXT CRASH ON THE SAME PATH ----------
# Found while auditing the training-completion teardown for further Null dereferences after
# the StopChannels fix above. TEngine.EndMatch's LAST instruction before its epilogue is an
# indirect call through a function-pointer Global, and that Global is split from the one the
# match setup writes -- so the callback that tears the match down never runs.
# Grounded entirely in NSS5.exe, three byte-identical bodies, one address:
#   * TEngine.SetUpMatch (VA 0x004CE7BE, byte-identical 1776/1776) loads its 4th parameter
#     a3:Int() at 0x004CE7C4 (`mov ebx,[ebp+0x14]`) and stores it at 0x004CE860
#     `mov [0xc5b1c0], ebx` -- a plain dword store with NO refcount inc/dec, which is what a
#     value type (function pointer) looks like and what an object store never looks like
#     (codegen-patterns 10.6). That store is the recovered line `g_engine_int12 = a3`.
#   * TEngine.SetUpReplay (VA 0x004CEEAE, byte-identical 623/623) stores its 2nd parameter
#     a1:Int() into the SAME address at 0x004CEEBA `mov [0xc5b1c0], eax` (eax = [ebp+0xc]),
#     and spells it g_engine_fnend. Its header names the slot outright:
#     "0x00C5B1C0 g_engine_fnend:Int() -- a FUNCTION-POINTER Global (same one the corpus
#     already calls through); a1 is stored straight in".
#   * TEngine.EndMatch (VA 0x004D732F, byte-identical 530/530) READS it at 0x004D752F
#     `call dword ptr [0xc5b1c0]`, the instruction immediately before `mov eax,0` and the
#     epilogue. Its header likewise states "g_engine_fnend:Int() 0x00C5B1C0 -- a
#     FUNCTION-POINTER Global, `call [0xC5B1C0]` with no arguments and no receiver."
#   Corroborated by two generated tables that were never consulted for the above:
#     extracted/globals_final.tsv:98 gives `0x00c5b1c0 Int g_engine_int12 ... 2 writes`
#     (the two stores are exactly SetUpMatch's and SetUpReplay's), and
#     extracted/call_sites.tsv:9216 gives `0x004d732f 0x004d752f ct 0x00c5b1c0`.
#   global_address_map.tsv left BOTH names AMBIGUOUS ("no alignment forced it") because a
#   function-pointer Global generates no [ptr] load the aligner recognises -- the same blind
#   spot global_address_adjudicated.tsv:110 already documents for this very Global in
#   TEngine.SetUpReplay ("the aligner only finds 9 machine touches for [10 globals] because
#   g_engine_fnend (a Int()-function-pointer Global) generates no [ptr]/[...] access").
# WHAT THE SPLIT COSTS, MEASURED. Every match and every training is set up through
# SetUpMatch, so in normal play the callback lands in g_engine_int12 and g_engine_fnend
# keeps whatever SetUpReplay last put there -- which, if no replay has run, is nothing.
# BlitzMax initialises an unassigned function-pointer Global to a stub that raises
# TNullFunctionException, "Attempt to call uninitialized function pointer"
# (mod/brl.mod/blitz.mod/blitz.bmx:107). status/debugruns/20260822-204758/globals.tsv shows
# that stub's address plainly: g_co_fn1, g_co_fn2, g_hookfn, g_kits_cancelfunc, g_kits_fn,
# g_kits_okfunc, g_kits_quitfn, g_league_setround and g_engine_fnend ALL hold $007a428c,
# while g_engine_int12 holds $006fd95f -- the real callback SetUpMatch stored. So
# `g_engine_fnend()` at EndMatch is a call into the null-function stub and throws, one
# statement past the StopChannels crash the block above fixes. Same run, same function.
# Semantics agree with the addresses independently. For a training the callback is
# TTraining.ClearUpTraining (TTraining:41179 passes it as SetUpMatch's a3), and that is the
# body that sets g_intraining = 0, blanks g_traininglabel1..4 and applies
# g_profile.UpdateEnergy(-20.0). With the split in place none of it runs, so even in a

# calls and twenty arr03[i].SelectItem calls all run through elements nothing ever wrote.

#      allocates the array), CreateScreen (which stores the ELEMENTS), and the reader(s).
#      Counts match our source use-for-use, e.g. 0x00C65CA4 has 40 references -- 1
#      module-body store, 18 in CreateScreen, 20 in RefreshKits, 1 in UpdateKitCmb.
#   2. Every element store in CreateScreen is `mov [eax+edi*4+0x18],ebx` (BBArray data at
#      +0x18) immediately after loading the slot, and the gadget NAME literal pushed into
#      the CreateCombo/CreateInputBox/CreateButton call just above it spells the writer's

#      order-free landmark: it does not rely on aligning reference lists at all.

#      table, independently gives arr02..arr11 the same addresses AND element types/sizes

column1: # ---- 2026-08-22 (w711): the sixteen match-stat counters -- THE SCOREBOARD READS
# ---- SIXTEEN VARIABLES NOTHING EVER INCREMENTS -------------------------------------
# TEngine.RenderScoreboard (VA 0x004D0AB3, byte-identical 7128/7128) draws the stats page
# from g_stat_<name>_h / g_stat_<name>_a. Not one of those sixteen names is written
# anywhere in the program, so every figure on the scoreboard's stats page is the literal
# string "0" for the whole match. Purely visual, never crashes, and invisible to the byte
# oracle -- the body is byte-perfect.
# THE ADDRESSES, AND WHY THE ALIGNMENT IS FORCED RATHER THAN GUESSED.
# The sixteen reads are sixteen `push dword ptr [abs32]` at these offsets from the body's
# VA, in this order:
# (e.g. 0x004D0EBF `ff3564b2c500 push dword ptr [0xc5b264]`, 0x004D1509
# `ff359cb2c500 push dword ptr [0xc5b29c]`.) The body's own read order is
#   shots_h shots_a ontarget_h ontarget_a corners_h corners_a offside_h offside_a
#   pens_h pens_a freekicks_h freekicks_a yellows_h yellows_a reds_h reds_a
# -- lines 136..172 of src/recovered/TEngine.RenderScoreboard.bmx, each pair drawn at
# xleft then xright. That order is NOT monotonic in the address (corners 0x27C/0x280 are
# read BEFORE offside 0x28C/0x290, which are read before pens 0x284/0x288, which are read
# before freekicks 0x274/0x278), and the push sequence has exactly the same three
# inversions in exactly the same places. Sixteen for sixteen with a scrambled order is a
# pairing, not a coincidence. `xleft` before `xright` fixes _h as the lower address of
# each pair.
# THE WRITERS, AND WHY g_engine_int29..44 IS THE CANONICAL SPELLING.
# Byte-sweeping NSS5.exe for each little-endian dword finds every store. The zeroing pass
# is TEngine.ResetStats (0x004D7BA9, byte-identical 190/190): sixteen
# +149,+159,+169 walking 0xC5B264..0xC5B2A0 in strict address order, which our body spells
# g_engine_int29 .. g_engine_int44 in the same strict order after its two Float stores
# (g_engine_float07/08, the possession accumulators, which occupy the offsets below +19).
# Five more bodies increment the same slots under the SAME g_engine_intNN spelling:
#   TBall.Kick +2489        `add [0xc5b264],1`   g_engine_int29 / int30   (a shot)
#   TBall.Parry +204/+195   `add [0xc5b26c],1`   g_engine_int31 / int32   (on target)
#   TEngine.GoalScored +1667/+1692                g_engine_int31 / int32   (on target)
#   TEngine.SkipMatchTime +1362.. (the simulator) int29,30,31,32,33,34,35,36,39,40
# Six independent bodies against one, so g_engine_intNN is the corpus-wide spelling and
# the canonical here. extracted/global_address_map.tsv agrees and was already sure of it:
# every g_engine_intNN is STRONG or CERTAIN at exactly the address derived above, while
# every g_stat_* is AMBIGUOUS with no address at all. No co-occurrence risk: no recovered
# body declares a g_stat_* name and its g_engine_intNN partner together.
# THE SEMANTICS CROSS-CHECK EVERY PAIR INDEPENDENTLY OF THE ORDER ARGUMENT.
#   0xC5B264/68 incremented only where a shot is taken (TBall.Kick)         = shots
#   0xC5B26C/70 incremented on a save (TBall.Parry) and on a goal           = on target
#   0xC5B274/78, 27C/80, 284/88 all incremented inside TEngine.SetUpSetPiece = free kicks,
#              corners, penalties -- the three set-piece kinds
#   0xC5B28C/90 incremented only in TPlayer.CheckOffside                    = offside
#   0xC5B294/98 incremented only in TPlayer.YellowCard                      = yellows
#   0xC5B29C/A0 incremented only in TPlayer.RedCard                         = reds
# STILL SPLIT AFTER THESE ROWS, AND OUTSIDE THIS WORKER'S SLICE -- HANDED ON.
# Six of the sixteen slots carry a THIRD spelling, used by the one body that increments
# them, and those names are written so they never appear in dead_globals.py's list:
#   0xC5B28C/90  g_offside_home / g_offside_away   (TPlayer.CheckOffside)
#   0xC5B294/98  g_homeYellows  / g_awayYellows    (TPlayer.YellowCard)
#   0xC5B29C/A0  g_redcards_home/ g_redcards_away  (TPlayer.RedCard)
# Each of those six must also be merged into its g_engine_intNN, or the card and offside
# counters will still be incremented into a variable neither ResetStats nor the scoreboard
# ever touches. Not added here because their alias half lies outside this slice.

column1: # ---- 2026-08-22 (w711): the camera scroll limits -- READ FROM Engine.ini, THEN READ BACK
# ---- UNDER A DIFFERENT NAME (the g_ply_turnrate pattern again) ----------------------
# TEngine.SetUp (0x004CD9C3, byte-identical) parses Inc/Engine.ini and stores three values;
# TEngine.UpdateOffset and TEngine.UpdateOffsetReplay read the same three addresses under
# the placeholder names g_engine_int14/15/16 and get 0. They are the camera's pitch-edge
# clamp margins:
#     limita = (g_player_int16 + TPitch.YardsToPixels(g_engine_int14)) * zoom
#     limitb = (g_player_int17 + TPitch.YardsToPixels(g_engine_int15)) * zoom
#     limitc = (g_player_int17 + TPitch.YardsToPixels(g_engine_int16)) * zoom
# With the three at 0 the YardsToPixels term vanishes and the camera is clamped to the bare
# half-pitch rectangle instead of half-pitch + 50/44/26 yards of overscroll -- the view
# cannot follow play past the pitch edge, in the match camera AND in replays. Silent.
# THE STORES, AND THE KEY STRINGS THAT NAME THEM.
# TEngine.SetUp at +272..+405 is three identical ReadSettingFloat sequences: push 100.0
# (0x42C80000), push 0, push <key string>, push <ini path>, call 0x004BBFC1, then the
# Float->Int helper 0x005B9690 and a store of eax:
#   0x004CDAE3 `68f02fc700 push 0xc72ff0`  ...  0x004CDB03 `a3ecb1c500 mov [0xc5b1ec],eax`
#   0x004CDB0F `681430c700 push 0xc73014`  ...  0x004CDB2F `a3f0b1c500 mov [0xc5b1f0],eax`
#   0x004CDB3B `683c30c700 push 0xc7303c`  ...  0x004CDB5B `a3f4b1c500 mov [0xc5b1f4],eax`
# The three pushed strings decode out of NSS5.exe's data (BlitzMax string object: length at
# +8, UTF-16 payload at +12) as exactly "limitscrollx", "limitscrolly1", "limitscrolly2",
# and the fourth push 0xC721FC is "incbin::Inc/Engine.ini". src/recovered/TEngine.SetUp.bmx
# lines 131-133 are those three statements in that order, spelled g_limit_scroll_x /
# g_limit_scroll_y1 / g_limit_scroll_y2, and that file's own header already records
# "0x00C5B1EC g_limit_scroll_x:Int  0x00C5B1F0 g_limit_scroll_y1:Int  0x00C5B1F4

# is spelled out in full.
# TScreen_Negotiate.ButtonLower (0x0057A6BC, byte-identical 150/150) contains one statement
# `g_neg_a = g_player_p50`, and ButtonHigher (0x0057A752, 150/150) its twin

#       a1d4efc600   mov eax, dword ptr [0xc6efd4]     <- the RIGHT-HAND SIDE is LOADED
#       a344ccc600   mov dword ptr [0xc6cc44], eax     <- the LEFT-HAND SIDE is STORED
# so the assignment TARGETS are g_neg_a / g_neg_value = 0x00C6CC44, and the SOURCES are
# g_player_p50 / g_neg_base = 0x00C6EFD4. global_address_map.tsv has both pairs the other
# way round (g_neg_a 0x00C6EFD4 STRONG, g_player_p50 0x00C6CC44 STRONG), which is exactly
# what happens when a reference list is aligned in SOURCE order against machine order: in
# an assignment the RHS is loaded BEFORE the LHS is stored, so a one-statement body
# transposes. global_alias_unified.tsv then carried the error into two merges (row 658
# g_neg_a -> g_matchtime, row 560 g_player_p50 -> g_neg_base).
# WHAT THAT DOES TODAY, in the current build: nss5_assembled.bmx:40684 and :40704 read
# `g_matchtime = g_neg_base`. 0x00C6EFD4 is the global MilliSecs clock (CERTAIN in 5

# so every press of Lower or Higher on the negotiate screen ZEROES THE MATCH CLOCK -- with
# g_neg_base itself never written, the assignment stores 0 -- and the timestamp slot
# 0x00C6CC44 is never written at all, which is why its reader g_screen_negotiate_int03 is
# in the dead list. The two guards in Update, `g_matchtime > int03 + 500` and `+ 1000`
# (0x0057A812: `mov edx,[0xc6efd4]` / `mov eax,[0xc6cc44]` / `add eax,0x1f4` / `cmp edx,eax`),
# therefore compare the clock against 500 rather than against the moment of the click, so
# the pause between guesses does not happen.
# DIRECTION. 0x00C6CC44 keeps a writer's spelling; g_neg_value (ButtonHigher) is chosen over
# g_neg_a (ButtonLower) arbitrarily -- they are two spellings of one slot written by twin
# functions -- and the dead reader int03 joins it. 0x00C6EFD4 goes to g_matchtime, which is
# CERTAIN there and already the head of that 16-name group. No cycle: the override raises
# rank["=g_neg_value"] to 4, so assemble.py's de-alias pass drops the stale unified edge
# g_neg_value -> g_matchtime before the chain collapse, and g_matchtime is an alias in no

#   0x004CE888 `8d0534b2c500 lea eax,[0xc5b234]` / `50 push eax`
#   0x004CE88F `8d0530b2c500 lea eax,[0xc5b230]` / `50 push eax`
#   0x004CE896 `52 push edx` (Self) / `ff5050 call [eax+0x50]` = TFixture.GetFirstLegScore
# cdecl pushes RIGHT TO LEFT, so the FIRST push is the LAST argument: 0x00C5B234 is arg2 and
# 0x00C5B230 is arg1. SetUpMatch.bmx writes that call as
# `a0.GetFirstLegScore(Varptr g_engine_int23, Varptr g_engine_int24)`, so
# g_engine_int23 = 0x00C5B230 and g_engine_int24 = 0x00C5B234. extracted/addr_oracle.json's
# TEngine.MatchOver record is count-exact (4 names, 4 addresses) and pairs them the same way,
# independently.

# them g_engine_agg1/g_engine_agg2 -- CROSSED over relative to the int23/int24 numbering, and
# that is not a typo. Its reads are +147 [0xc5b230], +176 [0xc5b234], +303 push [0xc5b234],
# +398 push [0xc5b230]. Source lines 42-44 are
#   line 42 GetText(..) + " " + String(g_engine_agg1 + score1) + " - " + String(g_engine_agg2 + score2)
#   line 43 "(" + String(g_engine_agg1) + ") " + String(score1)

# emits agg2's operand first (+147 = 0xC5B230 = agg2) then agg1's (+176 = 0xC5B234 = agg1);

column1: # ---- 2026-08-22 (w711): the on-screen-message duration -- ONE CONSTANT, FIVE NAMES ------
# 0x00C5B1F8 holds the value 1750 in NSS5.exe's data image and is NEVER STORED TO anywhere
# in the program: a byte sweep for the dword finds 20 references across 11 functions
# (TEngine.SetUpSetPiece, UpdateSetPieceReady, GoalScored, DoHalfEnds, SaveReplay,
# DoYourSubstitutionOff, SkipMatchTime, TTeam.CheckComManagement, TPlayer.CheckOffside,
# RedCard, YellowCard) and every single one is a read. It is the duration argument of
# TScreenMessage.Create, i.e. how long a match message stays on screen.
# Because there is no writer instruction, this is codegen-patterns 21.1's "uncaptured
# initialiser" shape rather than a normal split -- and the corpus already carries the value:
# g_engine_int17 is declared `'!Global g_engine_int17:Int = 1750` by eight bodies and
# g_msg_style the same by one. The three names below are further readers of the same slot
# with no initialiser of their own, so they sit at 0 and their messages flash for 0 ms.
# Merging them onto g_engine_int17 both fixes the value and removes three Globals; nothing
# needs an initialiser added.
# The pairing is read straight off the argument pushes, no ordering assumption needed:
# TScreenMessage.Create is `(i,i,$,i,:TBitmapFont,:TImage,f,$)` and cdecl pushes right to
# left, so the run `push "FFFFFF" / push / push / push / push /
# push <text>` puts the duration exactly two pushes before the message text every time.
# STILL SPLIT AFTER THESE ROWS: g_msg_style (TPlayer.CheckOffside) is a fifth name for
# 0x00C5B1F8. It is not dead -- its pragma carries `= 1750` -- so it never appears in
# dead_globals.py and is out of this slice; it should be merged too.
0x00C5B1F8

column1: # ---- 2026-08-22 (w711): the pass and lob power ratios -- EVERY PASS HAS ZERO POWER ------
# TPlayer.TapKick sets `Self.kickpower = Self.distancetoteammate * <ratio>` and the ratio is
# one of four Engine.ini kickdistratio_* values. Two of the four are read under placeholder
# names that nothing writes, so kickpower is computed as distance * 0.0 on those paths --
# the pass or lob is played with no power at all. Same failure shape as the already-fixed
# g_player_float05 (velocity * 0.0).
# THE FOUR SLOTS, FROM THE KEY STRINGS. TPlayer.SetUp emits six consecutive ReadSettingFloat
# calls whose key push and x87 store are 18 bytes apart:
#   0x004ED228 push 0xC79138 "energydrain"          -> 0x004ED23A fstp [0xc5de90]
#   0x004ED24A push 0xC7915C "kickdistratio_shoot"  -> 0x004ED25C fstp [0xc5de94]
#   0x004ED26C push 0xC79190 "kickdistratio_lob"    -> 0x004ED27E fstp [0xc5de98]
#   0x004ED28E push 0xC791C0 "kickdistratio_pass"   -> 0x004ED2A0 fstp [0xc5de9c]
#   0x004ED2B0 push 0xC791F0 "kickdistratio_cross"  -> 0x004ED2C2 fstp [0xc5dea0]
# matching TPlayer.SetUp.bmx:264-267 g_player_kickratioshoot / kickratiolob / kickratiopass /
# kickratiocross in that order. Each key string was decoded out of the pushed BlitzMax string
# object, so the pairing does not rest on statement ordering.
# TPlayer.TapKick's own header independently states "g_player_float18/19/20/21:Float
# (0x00C5DE94/98/9C/A0, pass-power multipliers)", and the body's semantics agree slot for
# slot: `kicktype = 2 ... * g_player_float18` (shoot), `kicktype = 3 ... * g_player_float19`
# (lob), `kicktype = 1 ... * g_player_float20` (pass). float18 and float21 are already merged;
# these two are the remainder.
0x00C5DE98
column2: g_player_float19
column4: Sole writer TPlayer.SetUp 0x004ED27E `d91d98dec500 fstp dword ptr [0xc5de98]`, 18 bytes after `push 0xC79190` = "kickdistratio_lob" (TPlayer.SetUp.bmx:265). TapKick (0x004F7528, byte-identical 1889/1889) reads it as `d80d98dec500 fmul dword ptr [0xc5de98]` at +1129/+1399/+2280 etc., always under `kicktype = 3` (the lob). global_address_map.tsv has g_player_kickratiolob STRONG at 0x00C5DE98 and TapKick's header names 0x00C5DE98 as g_player_float19. Engine.ini kickdistratio_lob=0.15; at 0.0 every lob is played with kickpower 0.

column4: The interface font array. Its only WRITE is the module body's array allocation at 0x004BA897; TScreen.SetUpFonts fills the elements (`g_fonts[0]`/`g_fonts[1]` = LoadFontChecked) and reads the slot at +73..+289, and six other bodies read it under the same name. global_address_map.tsv has g_fonts CERTAIN at 0x00C61710, forced in 5 bodies, unanimous. The dead read is TScreen.SetUp +4 `a11017c600 mov eax, dword ptr [0xc61710]` followed by `8b4018 mov eax,[eax+0x18]` and a compare against 0x5C9C80 (bbNullObject) -- BBArray data at +0x18, element 0, i.e. the body's `If Not g_gadget_arr[0]`. That guard is the once-only initialiser for the fonts, the default background, the cursor and the two UI sounds; split, g_gadget_arr[0] is Null forever, so the block re-runs on every TScreen.SetUp call and reloads all five assets each time. Type note: the dead declaration is Object[4] and the canonical is TImageFont[]; extracted/module_globals_decoded.tsv already records the module-body declaration as TImageFont with 4 elements and calls the Object[] pragma "a refinement, not a conflict".

column1: # ---- 2026-08-22 (w711): g_matchprep_iconshinpads -- SUPERSEDES THE "NOT MERGED" NOTE -----
# The "NOT MERGED : g_matchprep_iconshinpads (0x00C68584)" block earlier in this file
# concluded "the LoadImageChecked calls for this icon group have not been reconstructed
# anywhere. Genuinely unwritten; do not invent a row." That was true when it was written and
# is not true now: TScreen_MatchPrep.CreateScreen has since moved to src/recovered/ and
# lines 143-152 load the whole icon group, and two of its siblings were merged in the
# meantime (global_alias_adjudicated.tsv rows 40/41: 0x00C6857C icondrugs -> g_img_drugsboost,
# 0x00C68580 iconbooze -> g_img_boozeboost).
# THE LAYOUT, READ OFF THE ORIGINAL. CreateScreen loads the icons as ten
# `push <path literal> / <concat with g_mediapath> / call 0x004BC372 LoadImageChecked /
# release old / mov [target], ebx` groups, each store belonging to the push that precedes
# its own call. Decoding each pushed BlitzMax string gives:
#   0x0055C262 push 0xC8C294 "ShinPadsBoost.png" -> 0x0055C296 mov [0xc68584], ebx
#   0x0055C29E push 0xC8C2C4 "ShinPads28.png"    -> 0x0055C2D2 mov [0xc6859c], ebx
#   0x0055C2DA push 0xC8C2EC "BootBoost.png"     -> 0x0055C30E mov [0xc68588], ebx
#   0x0055C316 push 0xC85D14 "Boot28.png"        -> 0x0055C34A mov [0xc685a0], ebx
# So the slot layout is two contiguous runs -- the *Boost icons at 0x7C/0x80/0x84/0x88/0x8C
# and the *28 icons at 0x94/0x98/0x9C/0xA0/0xA4 -- and the two already-adjudicated anchors
# (0x7C = drugsboost, 0x80 = boozeboost) sit exactly where that layout predicts, which is
# the independent control on the push/store pairing. 0x00C68584 is therefore the SHINPADS
# BOOST icon, not the 28px one, and that is also what the reader wants: SetUpScreen:245 is
# `g_matchprep_bartackling.SetBoostIcon(g_matchprep_iconshinpads, shinboost)`.

column2: g_matchprep_iconshinpads
column4: TScreen_MatchPrep.CreateScreen stores LoadImageChecked(g_mediapath + "ShinPadsBoost.png") here at 0x0055C296 `891d8485c600 mov dword ptr [0xc68584], ebx`, 52 bytes after its own `68 94c2c800 push 0xc8c294` -- and CreateScreen.bmx:147 spells that statement g_img_shinpadsboost. The only other reference to 0x00C68584 in NSS5.exe is the dead read TScreen_MatchPrep.SetUpScreen +3883 `ff358485c600 push dword ptr [0xc68584]`, one instruction after `a1d885c600 mov eax,[0xc685d8]` loads the tackling bar as the receiver -- i.e. line 245's SetBoostIcon. SetUpScreen's own header lists "0x00C68584 iconshinpads". g_img_shinpadsboost is declared by exactly one body so it cannot be double-booked. Supersedes the NOT MERGED note above, which predates CreateScreen's promotion to src/recovered/.

column1: # ---- 2026-08-22 (w730): the input layer. ONE FINDING THAT CANNOT BE A ROW -----------------
# NOT A ROW, DELIBERATELY. `g_options_controls` is the ONE name in the control block that is
# used for TWO DIFFERENT ADDRESSES, so the single row this file can express would be wrong
# whichever canonical it named. global_address_map.tsv already says so:
#     g_options_controls  -  AMBIGUOUS  Int[]  2  bodies disagree: 00c5d1dc:1 00c5d1fc:1
# assemble.global_alias_map() is keyed by NAME ({alias lower: canonical lower}) and
# apply_alias_map() rewrites the whole emitted text, so a row `g_options_controls ->
# g_options_arr07` fixes TOptions.NewButtonKick2 and simultaneously makes
# TOptions.NewButtonReplay store the REPLAY key into the PASS binding. That is strictly
# worse than the split. Recorded here so the next pass does not re-derive it and then write
# the harmful row.
# THE TWO SLOTS, MEASURED. Both bodies are byte-identical (46/46) and load their array
# Global into esi in the first instruction after the prologue:
#   TOptions.NewButtonKick2  VA 0x004E495D, at 0x004E4962:
#       8b35dcd1c500   mov esi, dword ptr [0xc5d1dc]      -> 0x00C5D1DC
#   TOptions.NewButtonReplay VA 0x004E4A15, at 0x004E4A1A:
#       8b35fcd1c500   mov esi, dword ptr [0xc5d1fc]      -> 0x00C5D1FC
#   both then: 8b1da8d1c500 mov ebx,[0xc5d1a8] (= g_ctrl_player, the control-set index)
#              ff1554d5c500 call [0xc5d554] (TOptions+0x3c = GetNewControl)
#              89449e18     mov dword ptr [esi + ebx*4 + 0x18], eax   (BBArray data at +0x18)
# The canonicals are settled independently by TOptions.LoadOptions (VA 0x004E3AED,
# byte-identical 3308/3308), which fills the whole control block in ini-key order from
# 0x004E3B9D onwards: 0x00C5D1DC receives "k_Button2"/"j_Button2" and 0x00C5D1FC receives
# "k_Replay"/"j_Replay". global_address_map.tsv makes both CERTAIN:
#     g_options_arr07  0x00C5D1DC  CERTAIN  Int[]  forced in 3 bodies, unanimous
#     g_options_arr11  0x00C5D1FC  CERTAIN  Int[]  forced in 3 bodies, unanimous
# and the emitted build already reads BOTH under those names -- TJoy.Update, TEngine.CheckInput,
# TOptions.SaveOptions, TScreen_Controls.RefreshButtons. Only the two writers are stranded.
# COST. `Global g_options_controls:Int[]` is emitted with NO SIZE and nothing ever reads it.
# status/debugruns/20260822-213034/globals.tsv captured it as literally `Null` during a real
# session (every sibling control array in the same dump is `alloc`), so
# `g_options_controls[g_ctrl_player] = GetNewControl()` indexes a Null BBArray: the store
# above resolves to linear address 0x18. Pressing CONTROLS -> "KICK 2" or "REPLAY" and then
# any key takes the process down; the pass-key and replay-key bindings can never be changed.
# Note this defect is INVISIBLE to scripts/dead_globals.py by construction -- that script
# lists read-never-written Globals, and this is the mirror case, written-never-read.
# THE FIX, for whoever may touch src/recovered. Rename the pragma AND the reference in the two
# bodies; per global_alias_map()'s own docstring the name a pass chooses is never load-bearing
# (each body is verified alone with one Global per '!Global pragma), so neither 46/46 moves:
#   src/recovered/TOptions.NewButtonKick2.bmx   g_options_controls -> g_options_arr07
#   src/recovered/TOptions.NewButtonReplay.bmx  g_options_controls -> g_options_arr11
# Doing only ONE of the two is enough to make a row legal for the other, but do both -- the
# name then disappears entirely. An initialiser on the pragma
# (`'!Global g_options_controls:Int[] = New Int[2]`) would only convert the crash into a
# silent no-op and must not be used as the fix.
# ALSO SEEN, NO ACTION. `g_options_arr09` is emitted `Int[2]`, allocated (the same dump shows
# it `alloc`), and referenced by nothing: 0x00C5D1EC's live name is g_opt_ctrlbutton4, already
# adjudicated in global_alias_adjudicated.tsv. Harmless orphan, listed so it is not mistaken
# for a fourth control array. And g_screen_float07/08 (0x00C7DB78/7C, TScreen.GetInput's idle
# stick xy) are dead in OURS and dead in the ORIGINAL alike: nothing in NSS5.exe writes either
# slot and both hold 00000000 in .data, so the 0.0 our build reads is the original's value.
# ---- 2026-08-22 (w731): ball actions -- ONE REAL BUG LEFT, AND THREE FALSE LEADS ---------
# Pre-emptive audit of PASSING / SHOOTING / SLIDE TACKLING. The pass/lob ratio pair
# (0x00C5DE98/9C) was already rowed above by w711 and I re-derived it independently from the
# key strings and confirmed it: a private emit (OUT_DIR to scratch, compile no-op'd) shows
# g_player_float19/20 gone and all 13 read sites resolving to the written
# g_player_kickratiolob / g_player_kickratiopass. Nothing further is needed for that one.
# Recorded here: one defect that is NOT an alias merge, and three dead Globals that look like
# the usual defect and are NOT, so nobody spends the afternoon on them again.
# (1) NEEDS AN INITIALISER, NOT A MERGE: g_player_double15 = 90.0.
# TPlayer.InterceptBall (0x004F9201, src/recovered_unverified -- report only, do not edit)
# ends its landing-spot test with `call 0x506049` (AngleDiff) at 0x004F9475 immediately
# followed by 0x004F947D `dd0548a0c700 fld qword ptr [0xc7a048]` and `dae9 fucompp`. The
# qword at 0x00C7A048 is a .data literal reading 90.0, so the original is
# `AngleDiff(...) > 90.0`. Our pragma InterceptBall.bmx:62 is a bare
# `'!Global g_player_double15:Double`, nothing writes 0x00C7A048 anywhere in NSS5.exe, and
# the emitted build declares `Global g_player_double15:Double` with no initialiser -- so the
# comparison runs against 0.0. AngleDiff(...,1) is non-negative, so the test is TRUE for
# every angle instead of only beyond a right angle: the interceptor always throws away the
# predicted landing point (`desx/desy = landing`) and falls back to the ball's CURRENT
# position, i.e. chasers never lead a moving ball. Fix is the initialiser on the pragma
# (`'!Global g_player_double15:Double = 90.0`), which InterceptBall.bmx:22 already records
# in prose ("Global 0x00C7A048 (double) g_player_double15=90.0") but never applied.
# The 20260822-213034 dump has g_player_double15 = 0.0, confirming it at runtime.
# (2) NOT BUGS -- three dead Floats whose ORIGINAL value is genuinely 0.0. Each is a .data
# float literal that got written down as a '!Global, so the emitted 0.0 is correct and an
# alias row would be actively wrong (there is no writer to merge with).
#   g_ball_float19  TBall.CheckAfterTouch 0x004C9DAB `d9053c27c700 fld dword ptr [0xc7273c]`
#                   -> [ebp-0x10]; 0xC7273C = 0.0. Original is `local_14 = 0.0` on the
#                   `distancetogoal_opp < YardsToPixels(18.0)` arm.
#   g_ball_float20  same body, 0x004C9E6E `d9054c27c700 fld dword ptr [0xc7274c]`, the
#                   `Case 0` arm of `g_engine_flag20 Mod 5`; 0xC7274C = 0.0.
#                   Both sit in the same sequential literal pool as the 0.25/0.75/1.0/315.0/
#                   45.0 constants the body already spells inline, which is the control.
#   g_training_dist TTraining.UpdatePassing 0x00580CF0 `d9052029c900 fld dword ptr [0xc92920]`
#                   seeding the `maxd` running maximum; 0xC92920 = 0.0 and the ADJACENT
#                   0xC92924 = 20.0 is the `maxd + 20.0` on the next line
#                   (0x00580D9F `d8052429c900 fadd dword ptr [0xc92924]`) -- a literal pair,
#                   not a Global pair. Seeding a max reduction at 0.0 is correct.
# (3) RULED CLEAN, for the record. Slide tackling is correct end to end: TPlayer.SlideBall
# (0x004F86D6) and TPlayer.BlockTackle (0x004F889E) reference NO module data Global except
# g_ball -- their reach `push 0x40400000` (3.0 yards), kickpowers 0x00C79EBC = 15.0 and
# 0x00C79EE4 = 5.0, and ClampFloat bounds +/-30.0 are all inline literals, so there is no
# operand for a dead Global to annihilate. TBall.Kick (0x004C91A2) dispatches every kicktype
# to the right Engine.ini pair, verified against TBall.SetUp's key strings:
